extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit leaders, social entrepreneurs, development and public-health practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for nonprofits on adopting corporate-style marketing and distribution models to increase reach and uptake of health and sanitation goods/services in remote areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from Coca-Cola's global marketing and distribution network
rubrics_metrics.description: What can nonprofits learn from mega-corporations like Coca-Cola, whose global network of marketers and distributors ensures that every remote village wants -- and can get -- an ice-cold Coke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use corporate-style networks (marketing + local distributors) as a model for reaching remote populations; consider how scalable, ubiquitous supply chains and marketing can be adapted to nonprofit goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design programs that create demand and ensure access
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that target communities both want and can get the product/service (phrased on the page as 'wants -- and can get -- an ice-cold Coke').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying corporate models to social goods, plan both demand-generation (marketing/education) and reliable last-mile distribution so interventions (health care, vaccinations, sanitation, condoms) are both desired and available.
